question: In 1859, with which physicist did Robert Wilhelm Bunsen invent flame spectroscopy, an instrument that allows elements to be identified by their emission spectra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gustav Robert Kirchhoff**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Robert Wilhelm Bunsen:

 
• Along with Gustav Robert Kirchhoff, he invented flame spectroscopy, an instrument that allows elements to be identified by their emission spectra.
 
• Based on that principle he further invented photometers and calorimeters.
 
• A photometer is used to measure the strength of electromagnetic radiation and a calorimeter is used to measure the volume and heat produced during a certain time interval.

**Flame Spectroscopy:**

 
• Also known as **flame photometry.**
 
• The main purpose is **to excite analyte atoms.**
 
• Based on the **Beer-Lambert law **that describes the** relationship between light absorption and concentration of the element. **
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **​**In the determination of the** alkali and alkaline earth metals.**
 
• Identifying the **proportion of Lead (Pb) in the Petrol.**
 
• Finding the** proportion of Calcium (Ca) and Magnesium (Mg) in the cement.****​**
